title: Modality vs. Morphology: A Framework for Time Series Classification for Biological Signals
abstract: arXiv:2605.18483v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Techniques for classifying biological signals are largely developed within specific modalities rather than the underlying signal structure (i.e., morphology), leading to disjointed methodologies and limited guidance across diverse signals. This work introduces a novel morphology--modality framework that connects waveform structure to a principled design of preprocessing, feature extraction, and modeling techniques for biological time-series classification. We analyze evidence across biological signals including electroencephalography, electromyography, electrocardiography, photoplethysmography, and ocular modalities including electrooculography, pupillometry, and eye-tracking, and organize according to their primary morphologies: spikes, bursts, oscillations, slow drift, and hierarchical rhythms. Across these categories, we examine how morphology influences the analytical pipeline from preprocessing to modeling and evaluation.

translated_title: 模态与形态：生物信号时间序列分类框架
translated_abstract: 生物信号的分类技术大多是在特定模态内开发的，而非基于底层的信号结构（即形态），这导致各方法之间彼此割裂，难以对多样化信号提供有效指导。本工作引入了一个新颖的形态—模态框架，将波形结构与生物时间序列分类中预处理、特征提取和建模技术的原则性设计相连接。我们分析了多种生物信号的相关证据，包括脑电图（EEG）、肌电图（EMG）、心电图（ECG）、光电容积描记（PPG），以及眼部模态（包括眼电图、瞳孔测量和眼动追踪），并根据其主要形态进行归类：尖峰、爆发、振荡、缓慢漂移和分层节律。在这些类别中，我们考察了形态如何影响从预处理到建模与评估的整个分析流程。
tldr: 本文提出一个形态—模态框架，将生物信号的波形结构（尖峰、爆发、振荡、缓慢漂移、分层节律）与时间序列分类的预处理、特征提取和建模设计原则相联系，突破了传统上按模态割裂开发分类方法的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel morphology-modality framework that connects the waveform structures of biological signals (spikes, bursts, oscillations, slow drift, and hierarchical rhythms) to principled design choices in preprocessing, feature extraction, and modeling for time series classification, overcoming the fragmentation of modality-specific methodologies.
